candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — serious adverse drug reaction and client teaching
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients taking lamotrigine to stop the medication and promptly contact the prescriber when a new rash appears because early benign and life-threatening rashes cannot be reliably distinguished.

options.A: Continue lamotrigine and report the rash only if blisters develop
options.B: Skip one dose, then restart at the same dose if the rash fades
options.C: Increase the dose more slowly while continuing the medication
options.D: Do not take another dose and contact the prescriber immediately for evaluation

candidate.rationale: Lamotrigine carries a boxed warning for life-threatening serious skin rashes, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis. Because benign and serious rashes cannot reliably be distinguished at onset, the current label directs that lamotrigine be discontinued at the first sign of rash unless the rash is clearly not drug related. Therefore D is the safest instruction pending clinical evaluation. A and C continue exposure despite the warning, and B proposes an unsupervised restart that is not supported by the label.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Lamotrigine can cause life-threatening serious rashes; it should be discontinued at the first sign of rash unless the rash is clearly not drug related, and restart after discontinuation for rash requires careful benefit-risk consideration.
